source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_45/training_0.csv"

# Target schema:

# Target examples show 3 rows with values mostly equal to the column names as integers or floats,

# - Age (int)
# - Item ID (int)
# - Item Name (string in source, but target expects integer)
# - Price (float in source, target expects integer for Price, but also float for Average Purchase Price and Total Purchase Value)

# Step 2: We need to create columns with suffixes _x and _y, and some aggregations:
# - Purchase Count: count of purchases per Gender
# - SN: appears as integer in target, but source SN is string, so we can count distinct SN per Gender or convert SN to integer if possible

agg_x = df0.groupby('Gender').agg(
    Purchase_Count=('Purchase ID', 'count'),
    SN_count=('SN', 'nunique'),  # SN as count of unique SN per Gender (to convert SN string to int)
    Age_x=('Age', 'median'),  # median age as integer
    Item_ID_x=('Item ID', 'median'),
    Item_Name_count=('Item Name', 'nunique'),  # count distinct item names as integer
    Price_x=('Price', 'median'),
    Purchase_ID_x=('Purchase ID', 'mean')  # mean purchase id as float, will convert to float later
).reset_index()

    'SN_count': 'SN',
    'Item_ID_x': 'Item ID_x',
    'Item_Name_count': 'Item Name',
    'Price_x': 'Price',
    'Purchase_ID_x': 'Purchase ID_x'
}, inplace=True)

# Convert appropriate columns to integer as target expects integer for these

agg_x['SN'] = agg_x['SN'].astype(int)

agg_x['Item Name'] = agg_x['Item Name'].astype(int)

agg_x['Purchase ID_x'] = agg_x['Purchase ID_x'].astype(float)  # target expects float

    Age_y=('Age', 'mean'),
    Item_ID_y=('Item ID', 'mean'),
    Average_Purchase_Price=('Price', 'mean'),
    Purchase_ID_y_int=('Purchase ID', 'sum')  # sum as integer
).reset_index()

# Rename columns to match target schema names for _y columns
agg_y.rename(columns={
    'Item_ID_y': 'Item ID_y',
    'Average_Purchase_Price': 'Average Purchase Price',
    'Purchase_ID_y_int': 'Purchase ID_y'
}, inplace=True)

# Convert Purchase ID_y to integer as target expects integer

# For final columns without suffix:

    Item_ID=('Item ID', 'median'),
    Total_Purchase_Value=('Price', 'sum')
).reset_index()

    'Item_ID': 'Item ID',
    'Total_Purchase_Value': 'Total Purchase Value'
}, inplace=True)

agg_final['Item ID'] = agg_final['Item ID'].round().astype(int)
